title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene (182810) on chromosome 9q34.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous SPTAN1 mutations in dominant HMN families; the HMND11 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature for the gene the paper names. The abstract itself does not state 9q34.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is a neurologic disorder in which degeneration of lower motor neurons causes slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs. Sensory function is largely spared. Onset is usually in childhood or adolescence.

checks.claim: HMND11 is a neurologic disorder in which degeneration of lower motor neurons causes slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Distal hereditary motor neuropathies are a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies hallmarked by a length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions degeneration of lower motor neurons but not slowly progressive distal weakness and atrophy.

checks.claim: In HMND11, distal muscle weakness and atrophy mainly affect the lower limbs.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract says the degeneration is length-dependent but does not say the lower limbs are mainly affected.

checks.claim: In HMND11, sensory function is largely spared.
checks.evidence_quote: axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons

checks.claim: Onset of HMND11 is usually in childhood or adolescence.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense mutations in alpha-II spectrin in three families with juvenile onset hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The title says juvenile onset; 'childhood or adolescence' is not specified.

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2023) described several unrelated families with autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy that began in childhood or adolescence. Affected individuals had slowly progressive weakness and wasting of the distal lower limbs, with foot deformities. Electrophysiologic studies showed a motor axonal neuropathy, and sensory involvement was absent or minimal.

checks.claim: Beijer et al. described several unrelated families with autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families
checks.explanation: Three unrelated dominant families. Note the paper is from 2019, not 2023.

checks.claim: In the families described by Beijer et al., distal hereditary motor neuropathy began in childhood or adolescence.
checks.evidence_quote: three families with juvenile onset hereditary motor neuropathy
checks.explanation: Juvenile onset is stated in the title.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the families described by Beijer et al. had slowly progressive weakness and wasting of the distal lower limbs.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe slowly progressive distal lower-limb weakness or wasting in the patients.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the families described by Beijer et al. had foot deformities.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention foot deformities.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in affected individuals in the families described by Beijer et al. showed a motor axonal neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not report electrophysiologic findings.

checks.claim: Sensory involvement was absent or minimal in affected individuals in the families described by Beijer et al.
checks.evidence_quote: hallmarked by a length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons
checks.explanation: Sensory sparing is given only as a general definition of dHMN, not as a finding in these patients.

paragraphs.text: The families reported by Beijer et al. (2023) showed autosomal dominant transmission of HMND11.

checks.claim: The families with HMND11 reported by Beijer et al. showed autosomal dominant transmission.
checks.evidence_quote: in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families
checks.explanation: Dominant transmission is stated. Note the paper is from 2019, not 2023.

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2023) found heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin, in affected members of families with juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy. The mutations segregated with the disorder in the families.

checks.claim: Beijer et al. found heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene in affected members of families with juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families
checks.explanation: Stated; juvenile onset is given in the title.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene encodes alpha-II spectrin.
The SPTAN1 nonsense mutations identified by Beijer et al. segregated with distal hereditary motor neuropathy in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: Variable penetrance was noted for these mutations in two of three families, and phenotype severity differs greatly between patients.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not explicitly report segregation and notes variable penetrance (unaffected carriers) in two families, so 'segregated with the disorder' is overstated.
